concept.name: audio_path_forensics_and_config_regression_2026_08_02
concept.aliases: "voices sound metallic", "audio vibration distortion", "browser audio suddenly worse", "pipewire undoing our work again", "filter-chain came back", "audio configs disappeared", "who is resampling my audio", "sink stuck at 48000", "44100 stream on 48000 clock", "how to prove the DSP patches are innocent", "audio forensics method", "clock.force-rate", "allowed-rates", "masked service resurrected"
concept.symptoms: Soft voices sound unnatural, slightly metallic, with faint vibration/distortion on the FF154 build — despite the media patches being verified correct. Instinct says "the DSP patches are broken" or "retune the constants."
concept.when_to_recall: ANY audio-quality regression on this machine. ALWAYS before touching DSP code or constants. Also after ANY bulk file cleanup/rename/scrub operation (the trigger that caused this incident), and whenever a systemd user service that was "dealt with" reappears.
concept.wrong_instinct: 1. Blaming the Firefox DSP patches and retuning them. The patches were byte-verified innocent BEFORE the real cause was found; retuning would have corrupted a correct implementation to compensate for an OS-layer fault. 2. Trusting "everything is fine" from a model (or a past session log) without re-verifying the LIVE system state. Configs are FILES; files die in cleanups; the system then reverts silently while every document still says it is fixed. This is the SECOND time the OS audio layer reverted (first: 2026-06-26). The June fix was real; its files were later eaten. 3. Diagnosing sound quality in the first minute after a live clock/rate switch — the switch itself glitches the running stream (we heard "loud vibrations" immediately after forcing 44100 mid-stream; same config minutes later, after the stream reopened, was clean).
concept.human_rationale:
LAYMAN — WHAT HAPPENED: The browser's sound enhancement was fine. The operating system's audio plumbing had been silently reset to factory settings: the three custom config files that tamed it were deleted — almost certainly by our own 16,000-occurrence "gorilla" name-purge, because the files were named 10-gorilla-*.conf — and a parasite helper process (filter-chain) that Debian's factory preset auto-revives had come back from the dead because the "weld" holding it off (a mask symlink) was also just a file in the same purged folder. Result: every song at 44.1 kHz was being converted to 48 kHz at stock quality on its way to the speakers. That conversion was the metallic edge. Restoring the configs (with purge-proof names) and re-welding the parasite fixed the sound. THE MORAL: a fix that lives in a file is only as permanent as the file. After any mass cleanup, re-check every fix that lives on disk.
DEVELOPER — THE FORENSIC TECHNIQUE (the thing to never forget): Layer-by-layer elimination, each layer PROVEN before moving down. Never skip to tuning.
L1. PROVE THE PATCHES (before suspecting them): (a) tree: for each patch, apply to pristine VANILLA copy, diff result vs LIVE tree — demand byte-identical (20/20 for 01.MEDIA on 2026-08-02). (b) binary: grep -a libxul.so for ADDED strings (present) AND for REMOVED vanilla strings (absent — the negative-space check a stale build cannot fake). NS_WARNING strings are compiled OUT of opt builds — their absence proves nothing. (c) runtime deps: vainfo profiles, LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME, pref defaults in StaticPrefList. L2. VERIFY THE OS LAYER AGAINST THE LESSONS (this is where the body was buried): ls ~/.config/pipewire/pipewire.conf.d/ pipewire-pulse.conf.d/ ~/.config/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/ systemctl --user is-enabled filter-chain.service # "masked" is the ONLY safe answer systemctl --user is-active filter-chain.service # enabled+active = regressed pw-metadata -n settings | grep -E 'clock.rate|allowed' L3. PHOTOGRAPH THE LIVE GRAPH while audio plays (evidence, not vibes): pw-dump > before.json; parse Nodes (media.class + negotiated Format.rate) and Links → the actual signal path. Two verdict tools: - LINK MAP: is the app stream linked DIRECTLY to the sink, or via an interloper node? - CPU SNIFF: a daemon with 21ms CPU over 26h processes NOTHING (filter-chain was present but inert — exonerated as active suspect; masked anyway as hygiene). The rate mismatch (Stream 44100 → Sink 48000) identifies the ONE live processor: the resampler inside the adapter, at stock quality (4). L4. MEASURE THE CONTENT before judging the DSP: yt-dlp the actual clip (--extractor-args "youtube:player_client=android" beats SABR lockouts), ffmpeg loudnorm (EBU R128: this ballad = -15 LUFS, LRA 13.7 = double-normal dynamics, whispers at -28 dBFS), windowed RMS percentiles, band-split with the DSP's OWN one-pole math at its OWN corner frequencies, then run the BIT-EXACT C++ chain (Padé FastTanh, 220/3500 xover, 1.8/1.4 gains, drive 0.4 blend 0.2, ×1.1 makeup, 0.9 knee) over the real samples. Result: whispers get +4.4 dB, loud gets +3.9 dB, intelligibility band (mid) gets +0.8 dB — the enhancer is a fixed tone control, not a loudness intelligence. Limiter engagement 0.138% = the browser limiter was NOT the metallic source. Media-element playback never touches AudioDestinationNode → that stage exonerated for YouTube too. L5. FIX MINIMALLY, SCRUB-PROOF: systemctl --user mask --now filter-chain.service # mask, NEVER just disable ~/.config/pipewire/pipewire.conf.d/10-unleashed.conf: # NO brand words in filenames context.properties = { default.clock.allowed-rates = [ 44100 48000 96000 192000 ] } ~/.config/pipewire/pipewire-pulse.conf.d/10-unleashed.conf: stream.properties = { resample.quality = 15 } DO NOT force audio.format in WirePlumber — unnecessary for this fix and it is the S24LE no-sinks trap. DO NOT restore quantum=4096 (192k-era tuning; ~85ms latency at 48k). L6. VERIFY WITH THE SAME CAMERA: pw-dump after.json → Sink rate == Stream rate (44100==44100) = resampler PROVABLY out of the path. Note: a running sink may hold its old rate while any other stream (even pavucontrol's peak meters) keeps the graph busy; `pw-metadata -n settings 0 clock.force-rate 44100` switches it live as an A/B lever — but expect transient glitches on the stream that was playing THROUGH the switch; retest after the stream reopens. Remove force-rate afterwards; allowed-rates auto-follow is the steady state. L7. LEVEL-MATCHED A/B for any remaining coloration question: render the exact DSP chain over the real song offline (testA_raw / testB_dsp / testC_dsp_levelmatched) and play through pw-play — same path, only variable is the math.
concept.execution_logic:
OUTCOME 2026-08-02: metallic edge + vibrations GONE with the OS layer repaired and zero changes to Firefox. The "loud vibrations" heard immediately post-switch were the mid-stream clock change itself (proven: identical config + same daemon uptime later = clean). Browser DSP exonerated for this symptom class.
STANDING RULES: 1. After ANY bulk rename/scrub/cleanup: re-verify every on-disk fix (configs, masks, symlinks). Add their paths to the tree-restore procedure. 2. systemd user units with preset=enabled resurrect from "disable". Only "mask" holds. Check with is-enabled (want: masked) AND is-active (want: inactive). 3. Critical config filenames must never contain scrub-target words. 4. OS layer before DSP constants — always. The patches' innocence is provable in minutes (L1); DSP retuning to mask an OS fault poisons a correct implementation. 5. Never diagnose audio quality during/just after a live rate switch.
EVIDENCE (all preserved): SECOND.BRAIN/Chroma.DB.and.Brain.xml/AUDIO.AUDIT.2026-08-02/ {AUDIO_GRAPH_EVIDENCE_2026-08-02.md, pw-dump.before.json, pw-dump.after.json, pw-dump.playing.json, AUDIT_PASS1_MECHANICAL.md, AUDIT_PASS2_VERDICTS.md}. A/B clips: scratchpad testA_raw.wav / testB_dsp.wav / testC_dsp_levelmatched.wav (whisper t=5.9s, loud t=34.5s, from the G1 test ballad (the clip the retired G1 brand traced to)).
RESOLVED SAME DAY: clock.force-rate retired 12:26 after owner confirmed clean sound (allowed-rates auto-follow is the steady state). A/B/C listening test completed (3 runs, silent system): DSP versions "sounded good", differences "minute" — chain EXONERATED for harshness; benefit subtle, per the measurements. Full lab method, code, numbers and the quiet-lifter design spec: [[dsp_ab_lab_measure_simulate_listen_2026_08_02]] + executable tool gorilla-firefox-toolkit/modules/dsp-ab-lab.py.
